<instructions>You are inside super.engineering. For app-managed worktrees/targets, explicit UI/session layout actions, browser control, and reviews, use documented `sc` commands by default; use another mechanism only when the human user explicitly requests that specific mechanism. Never expose local API internals. super.engineering orchestration is opt-in per human request. Enabling the feature only makes it available; it does not authorize its use. Requests for subagents, agents, delegation, parallel work, teams, workers, or similar standard agent language use the current provider's native subagent tools. Those words never authorize `sc agent`, `sc agents`, `sc team`, `sc layout`, or any other super.engineering orchestration command. If native subagent tools are unavailable, report that instead of substituting `sc` orchestration. Use `sc` orchestration only when the human user says orchestrate or orchestration, names another provider/model or multiple providers/models, or requests app-managed UI/session behavior such as a new tab, pane, view, split, side-by-side agents, or a visible session. An explicit request for native subagents always stays native. Before changing managed state, run `sc instructions <topic>`: workspaces -> `sc instructions workspace`; worktrees/branches -> `sc instructions worktree`; super.engineering orchestration -> `sc instructions orchestration`; sessions/layout -> `sc instructions layout`; reviews -> `sc instructions review`; browser control -> `sc instructions browser`. Run `sc instructions` to list all guides. Only mutate managed state for an outcome the human user explicitly requested; read-only discovery is allowed. `sc workspace create` may run only when the human user explicitly asks to create a workspace. Never infer authorization from setup, isolation needs, subagents, delegation, agents, parallel work, or missing capabilities. Do not infer setup state from branch or directory names. `sc worktree create` may run only when the human user explicitly asks to create a new worktree or new branch. Never infer authorization from the task, isolation needs, subagents, delegation, agents, parallel work, separate sessions, or missing capabilities. A session launched by `sc worktree create` must complete its launched task in the current worktree and must not run `sc worktree create` for that task; the app rejects it until the human user sends input in that session. Report any need for another worktree to the human user. Never use worktree creation for delegation.</instructions>

1 # Releasing Hey Reachy 2 3 Signed artifacts are produced locally; CI only publishes the GitHub release with 4 generated notes. Credentials never enter the repository or CI. 5 6 ## One-time setup 7 8 1. **App Store Connect API key** — App Store Connect → Users and Access → 9 Integrations → App Store Connect API → Team Keys, role **App Manager**. 10 Download the `.p8` once and write the credentials file: 11 12 ```bash 13 mkdir -p ~/.config/reachy-mini 14 cat > ~/.config/reachy-mini/release.env <<'CONF' 15 REACHY_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=XXXXXXXXXX 16 REACHY_ASC_KEY_ID=XXXXXXXXXX 17 REACHY_ASC_ISSUER_ID=xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx 18 REACHY_ASC_KEY_PATH=/Users/you/.config/reachy-mini/AuthKey_XXXXXXXXXX.p8 19 CONF 20 ``` 21 22 2. **App IDs and the App Group** — the first signed build with 23 `-allowProvisioningUpdates` registers the bundle ids 24 (`com.alexey1312.ReachyMini`, `.Widget`), but the 25 `group.com.alexey1312.ReachyMini` capability must be added by hand in 26 Xcode's Signing & Capabilities, once per App ID (app and widget separately, 27 iOS and macOS separately). `xcodebuild` cannot create it. 28 29 3. **App Store Connect app record** — My Apps → New App: 30 - Name: **Hey Reachy**; if taken, fall back to “Hey Reachy — robot remote”. 31 - Subtitle: **Control your Reachy Mini**. 32 - Bundle id `com.alexey1312.ReachyMini`. 33 - The description must state it is an unofficial client for Reachy Mini by 34 Pollen Robotics. A public TestFlight link goes through Beta App Review, so 35 the name is checked before any App Store submission. 36 - App Privacy: no data collected. The app talks to the robot on the local 37 network and to Hugging Face with the user's own OAuth session; nothing is 38 sent to the developer. 39 - Encryption: answered in the Info.plist (`ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption`), 40 ASC asks nothing per build. 41 42 4. **Developer ID Application certificate** (macOS) — Xcode → Settings → 43 Accounts → Manage Certificates → “+” → Developer ID Application. 44 45 5. **macOS ships through both channels**, so the Mac App Store one needs its own 46 signing assets besides the Developer ID certificate: Apple Distribution and 47 Mac Installer Distribution. `-allowProvisioningUpdates` creates them through 48 the Xcode account the same way it does for iOS. The app record already 49 carries a macOS platform beside the iOS one — `mise run asc -- versions list 50 --app 6799644194` shows both — so nothing has to be created in App Store 51 Connect. What is not automatic is the App Group: step 2 registers it per App 52 ID, and the macOS App ID is a separate one from the iOS App ID. 53 54 ## Each release 55 56 1. Bump `MARKETING_VERSION` in `Apps/Project.swift` (bare semver, e.g. `0.2.0`) 57 and land it on `main`. Build numbers are the commit count — nothing to bump. 58 2. Tag and push; the tag triggers the GitHub release with git-cliff notes: 59 60 ```bash 61 git tag 0.2.0 && git push origin 0.2.0 62 ``` 63 64 3. Produce and ship the artifacts: 65 66 ```bash 67 mise run release:ios # archive → TestFlight 68 mise run release:macos # archive → both macOS channels (see below) 69 gh release upload 0.2.0 Apps/DerivedData/Export/macOS/HeyReachy-0.2.0.zip 70 ``` 71 72 `release:macos` archives once and exports that archive twice, because 73 `-exportArchive` re-signs per method — the two artifacts are the same build: 74 75 | Channel | Method | Artifact | Ends up in | 76 | -------------- | ----------------- | ---------------------------------- | ----------------------- | 77 | `developer-id` | notarize → staple | `Export/macOS/HeyReachy-.zip` | GitHub release, by hand | 78 | `appstore` | upload | `.pkg` (not kept) | TestFlight for macOS | 79 80 Developer ID runs first on purpose: it is the artifact that always ships, and a 81 failed App Store upload should not also cost you the zip. Pick one channel with 82 `--channel appstore` or `--channel developer-id`. 83 84 Both archive commands compile with the Xcode compilation cache off 85 (`COMPILATION_CACHE_ENABLE_CACHING=NO`) and then run 86 `Scripts/check-appintents-metadata.sh` against the archive before anything is 87 exported or uploaded. The intents live in a static SPM library, so the 88 Shortcuts app only ever sees what `appintentsmetadataprocessor` extracted into 89 `Metadata.appintents` — and extraction failing is a warning, never a build 90 error. TestFlight 0.1.1 shipped exactly that way: green archive, no actions in 91 the Shortcuts app. The check names every missing action instead; if it fails, 92 the fix is in the build, not in App Store Connect. 93 94 Dry runs: `mise run release:ios -- --no-upload` exports an `.ipa` without 95 uploading; `mise run release:macos -- --no-notarize` stops the Developer ID 96 channel after the signed export, and `--no-upload` makes the App Store channel 97 leave a `.pkg` in `Export/macOS/AppStore` instead of uploading it. Each flag 98 belongs to one channel and is ignored by the other. 99 100 ### When `-exportArchive` fails 101 102 Two failures land on the same step and have nothing to do with each other. 103 104 `productbuild failed` with `CSSMERR_CSP_USER_CANCELED` in the distribution log is 105 the keychain: the Mac Installer identity lives in `reachy-signing.keychain-db`, 106 and macOS put up an access dialog that a non-interactive run cannot answer — it 107 "cancels" itself after a few minutes. Authorize the key once and the keychain 108 keeps it: 109 110 ```bash 111 KC=~/Library/Keychains/reachy-signing.keychain-db 112 PW="$(cat ~/.config/reachy-mini/signing/keychain.pw)" 113 security unlock-keychain -p "$PW" "$KC" 114 security set-key-partition-list -S apple-tool:,apple:,codesign: -s -k "$PW" "$KC" 115 ``` 116 117 `Failed to Use Accounts` is the Xcode account instead, and only the upload leg 118 needs one. Export locally and hand the artifact to the API key, which does the 119 upload, the group and the Beta App Review submission in one call: 120 121 ```bash 122 mise run asc -- publish testflight --app 6799644194 --platform IOS \ 123 --ipa "Apps/DerivedData/Export/iOS/Hey Reachy.ipa" \ 124 --group c48f6abb-c178-40a2-8747-b6513add766e \ 125 --wait --test-notes "…" --locale en-US --submit --confirm 126 ``` 127 128 A macOS `.pkg` is not a zip, so `asc` cannot read the version out of it: that one 129 also needs `--version` and `--build-number` (the commit count) spelled out. 130 131 ## The store listing 132 133 The App Store copy lives in this repository, at `metadata/` — `app-info/en-US.json` 134 for the fields that belong to the app (name, subtitle, privacy policy URL) and 135 `version//en-US.json` for the ones that belong to a version (description, 136 keywords, promotional text, support and marketing URLs). Edit those, then: 137 138 ```bash 139 mise run asc -- metadata validate --dir ./metadata 140 mise run asc -- metadata push --app 6799644194 --version 0.2.0 --platform IOS --dir ./metadata --dry-run 141 mise run asc -- metadata push --app 6799644194 --version 0.2.0 --platform IOS --dir ./metadata 142 ``` 143 144 Push once per platform — `IOS` and `MAC_OS` carry separate version localizations 145 off the same files. `whatsNew` is deliberately absent: Apple refuses it on an 146 app's **first** App Store version (`Attribute 'whatsNew' cannot be edited at this 147 time`), so release notes start with the second one. 148 149 Everything that is not a localization is set once and stays: category, content 150 rights, age rating, availability, price, and the reviewer contact and notes. They 151 are listed by `asc validate --app 6799644194 --version-id --platform

`, 152 which is the one command worth running before every submission — it prints an 153 ordered remediation plan and exits non-zero while anything is missing. 154 155 Two of those answers are judgement calls, and both were decided against the two 156 Reachy apps already on the store rather than from first principles. Pollen's own 157 `Reachy Mini` (id 6766823749) sells the same community app catalogue this one 158 does — "browse and launch community apps instantly" — and stands at **9+** with 159 _Infrequent/Mild Cartoon or Fantasy Violence_ and _Mature/Suggestive Themes_, 160 which is a statement about what a community app might do rather than about the 161 app's own content. The independent `Reachy's Brain` (id 6757115923) is **4+** 162 with no advisories, but it ships no catalogue at all, so it is not the precedent 163 to copy. Hence: `USES_THIRD_PARTY_CONTENT`, because the Apps tab renders a Hugging 164 Face catalogue this project does not own, and every age-rating answer left at 165 `NONE` with an explicit `--age-rating-override-v2 NINE_PLUS` on top — declaring a 166 shelf position rather than asserting content the app does not contain. Both are 167 one `asc` command to revert. Their public halves are readable without a session: 168 `curl -s "https://itunes.apple.com/lookup?id="` carries 169 `contentAdvisoryRating`, `advisories` and `genres`; the content-rights 170 declaration is private and cannot be checked this way. 171 172 ## The public beta 173 174 `https://testflight.apple.com/join/CGjefT9a` — the **Public Beta** group, 175 `c48f6abb-c178-40a2-8747-b6513add766e`, capped at 500 testers. The link is in 176 the README; raising the cap is one `groups edit --public-link-limit`, lowering 177 it below the people who already joined is not. 178 179 Uploading is not distributing. An upload reaches the internal group by itself, 180 because `Internal` carries `hasAccessToAllBuilds`; the public group has to be 181 attached per build, per platform, and each one is its own Beta App Review: 182 183 ```bash 184 mise run asc -- builds add-groups --app 6799644194 --latest --platform IOS \ 185 --group c48f6abb-c178-40a2-8747-b6513add766e --submit --confirm 186 mise run asc -- builds add-groups --app 6799644194 --latest --platform MAC_OS \ 187 --group c48f6abb-c178-40a2-8747-b6513add766e --submit --confirm 188 mise run asc -- testflight review submissions list --build-id "" 189 ``` 190 191 What review reads lives at the app level, not the build level, so it is written 192 once and stays: the tester-facing text in `testflight app-localizations` 193 (description, feedback email, marketing URL, and the privacy policy at 194 `docs/privacy.md` — which has to resolve on `main`, or review fails on a 404), 195 and the reviewer-facing contact and notes in `testflight review edit`. The notes 196 carry the thing no reviewer can guess — that the app needs a robot nobody at 197 Apple has, that the Bluetooth sheet auto-presenting on first launch hides the 198 Local Network alert underneath it, and that Hugging Face sign-in is the one path 199 that completes without hardware. Beta App Review has no demo account to give, 200 because the app has no accounts. 201 202 Testers see the same What to Test note per build: 203 204 ```bash 205 mise run asc -- builds test-notes create --build-id "" \ 206 --locale en-US --whats-new "..." 207 ``` 208 209 ## Querying App Store Connect 210 211 `mise run asc` is the App Store Connect CLI with the same key already loaded — 212 `Scripts/asc.sh` maps the `REACHY_ASC_*` values onto the `ASC_*` names the tool 213 reads, so nothing is stored twice and no keychain profile exists to drift. 214 Everything after `--` goes to `asc`: 215 216 ```bash 217 mise run asc -- apps list 218 mise run asc -- builds list --app 6799644194 # did the TestFlight upload land? 219 mise run asc -- testflight beta-groups list --app 6799644194 220 ``` 221 222 `asc` resolves a stored profile before the environment, so an `asc auth login` 223 run by hand silently outranks this wrapper — `mise run asc -- auth status` 224 prints which of the two is answering. The key is App Manager, not Admin, so the 225 same limit release-ios.sh documents applies: it can read and submit, and it 226 cannot manage provisioning profiles. 227 228 The CLI also ships 23 agent skills (`asc install-skills`, pinned to a reviewed 229 commit) covering TestFlight, metadata, submissions and signing. 230 231 ## Xcode Cloud (optional, continuous TestFlight) 232 233 `Apps/ci_scripts/ci_post_clone.sh` makes a generated project buildable on 234 Xcode Cloud: it installs the pinned tools through the committed `bin/mise` 235 bootstrap, generates the workspace, and stamps `CI_BUILD_NUMBER` in as the 236 build number. Signing there is managed by Apple — no certificates leave the 237 account — and TestFlight distribution is a post-action checkbox. The setup 238 quirks (create the workflow from a local Xcode, start the build counter above 239 the last local upload, Git LFS is unsupported so never build the snapshot 240 scheme there) are commented at the top of the script. 241

2	name: verify-testflight-upload
3	description: "How to confirm a TestFlight upload actually landed — altool has no --list-builds, ask the ASC API via `mise run asc`"
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project
7	  originSessionId: 6b24408d-af71-4d7e-b5f9-f5bfff5acd21
8	  modified: 2026-08-10T10:28:30.506Z
9	---
10	
11	`mise run release:ios` prints "Uploaded build N" even when xcsift has already
12	reported `status: incomplete`, so that line is not evidence. `xcrun altool
13	--list-builds` does not exist (Xcode 26.4.1 altool 26.30.4 — only upload,
14	validate, list-apps, list-providers). Ask the App Store Connect API instead:
15	
16	```bash
17	mise run asc -- builds list --app 6799644194   # Hey Reachy; --limit N to trim
18	```
19	
20	Added 2026-08-10. This replaces the hand-signed ES256 JWT script that used to be
21	the only way in (`uv run --with pyjwt --with cryptography …`) — `asc` signs the
22	token itself from the same `~/.config/reachy-mini/release.env` key, mapped onto
23	`ASC_*` by `Scripts/asc.sh`. Reach for the raw API only for routes `asc` lacks.
24	
25	Two API details that cost a round trip each: the "What to Test" field is
26	`whatsNew` on `betaBuildLocalizations` (not `whatsToTest`, which 409s), and
27	`GET /builds/{id}/betaGroups` is forbidden — read `hasAccessToAllBuilds` on the
28	group instead to tell whether a build already reached the testers.
29	
30	**An internal group is never assigned a build, and trying is an error, not a
31	no-op:** `asc builds add-groups --build-id … --group <internal>` fails with
32	"Builds cannot be assigned to this internal group." ASC distributes every build
33	to internal testers by itself. So there is no assignment step to perform after
34	an upload — the positive signal is `Internal State = IN_BETA_TESTING` from
35	`mise run asc -- builds build-beta-detail view --build-id …`, which also shows
36	`External State` (`READY_FOR_BETA_SUBMISSION` until a Beta App Review). Note the
37	subcommand is `build-beta-detail view`, and listing/inspecting a build is
38	`builds info`, not `builds view`.
39	
40	**Why:** a green exit code from the release script proves nothing, because the
41	xcsift pipe hides the real xcodebuild result on long runs.
42	
43	**How to apply:** after any `release:ios`, read the build number and
44	`processingState` back from the API before telling the user it shipped.
45	
46	Related: [[deploy-visual-fixes-to-device]], [[asc-cli-wiring]]

11	From 2026-08-11 to 2026-08-12 no Apple ID was signed into Xcode on this machine
12	(`defaults read com.apple.dt.Xcode` → `DVTDeveloperAccountManagerAppleIDLists →
13	IDE.Identifiers.Prod = ()`). The user signed back in on 2026-08-12, **after** the
14	0.2.0 archives were already made, so the symptom may not reappear — but the
15	detour below is what shipped 0.2.0 and is now written into `docs/release.md`.
16	
17	Archiving and a local export never needed the account; only the upload leg did:
18	`-exportArchive` with `destination: upload` fails with `Failed to Use Accounts`
19	at `IDEDistributionUploadAccountStep`. The Mac Installer Distribution certificate
20	that was also missing then now exists, in its own
21	`~/Library/Keychains/reachy-signing.keychain-db` — see
22	[[signing-keychain-needs-partition-list]], which is the failure that replaced it.
23	
24	**Why:** `Scripts/release-env.sh` deliberately withholds the ASC API key from
25	`xcodebuild` (an App Manager key turns the flags into cloud signing, which it is
26	not entitled to do), so the upload leg has no credential to fall back on.
27	
28	**How to apply:** export locally, then upload with the key. Copy
29	`Scripts/exportOptions/appstore.plist`, `plutil -replace destination -string export`,
30	run `-exportArchive` against the existing archive, then one
31	`asc publish testflight --app 6799644194 --platform IOS|MAC_OS --ipa <file>
32	--group c48f6abb-c178-40a2-8747-b6513add766e --wait --test-notes … --locale en-US
33	--submit --confirm`, which uploads, attaches the public group and submits Beta App
34	Review together. A macOS `.pkg` is not a zip, so asc cannot read its version:
35	add `--version` and `--build-number` there. See [[asc-cli-wiring]],
36	[[verify-testflight-upload]], [[device-build-signing]].

2	name: asc-cli-wiring
3	description: "Where the App Store Connect CLI lives on this machine — mise pin, env mapping, and why its skills need a symlink"
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project

10	
11	Added 2026-08-10. `asc` (rorkai/App-Store-Connect-CLI) is pinned in `mise.toml`
12	as `"github:rorkai/App-Store-Connect-CLI[bin=asc]"` and driven through
13	`mise run asc -- <args>` (`Scripts/asc.sh`), which maps `REACHY_ASC_KEY_ID` /
14	`_ISSUER_ID` / `_KEY_PATH` from `~/.config/reachy-mini/release.env` onto the
15	`ASC_KEY_ID` / `ASC_ISSUER_ID` / `ASC_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH` the tool reads. **No
16	keychain profile was created on purpose** — `asc` resolves a stored profile
17	*before* the environment, so a later `asc auth login` would silently outrank the
18	file and start a second copy of the credentials drifting.
19	
20	`asc install-skills` writes its 23 skills to **`~/.agents/skills/`**, not
21	`~/.claude/skills/`, so Claude Code cannot see them until each is symlinked
22	across — the same bridge `xcode-disk-cleanup` already uses. Re-running the
23	installer after an `asc` upgrade refreshes the targets, not the symlinks.
24	
25	**Why:** the credentials existed long before the tool did, in a file outside
26	every worktree; duplicating them into a keychain would make "which key answered"
27	unanswerable.
28	
29	**How to apply:** query App Store Connect with `mise run asc -- …` rather than
30	hand-signing a JWT; if `asc` starts reporting a profile in `auth status`, someone
31	ran `auth login` and the wrapper is no longer the source of truth.
32	
33	Related: [[verify-testflight-upload]], [[device-build-signing]]

1	#!/bin/bash
2	# Archive the iOS app (Release, signed) and upload it to TestFlight.
3	#
4	#   mise run release:ios              # archive → upload to App Store Connect
5	#   mise run release:ios -- --no-upload   # archive → export an .ipa locally
6	#
7	# Signing and uploading go through the Xcode account, not the App Store Connect
8	# API key — see release-env.sh for the measurement behind that.
9	#
10	# The build number is the commit count: monotonic, reproducible, and never
11	# stored in the repository — so releasing does not require a version-bump
12	# commit for anything but MARKETING_VERSION.
13	set -euo pipefail
14	
15	# shellcheck source=Scripts/release-env.sh
16	. "$(dirname "$0")/release-env.sh"
17	
18	upload=true
19	require_development_team
20	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
21	  case "$1" in
22	  --no-upload) upload=false ;;
23	  *)
24	    echo "usage: release-ios.sh [--no-upload]" >&2
25	    exit 2
26	    ;;
27	  esac
28	  shift
29	done
30	
31	BUILD_NUMBER="$(git rev-list --count HEAD)"
32	ARCHIVE=Apps/DerivedData/Archives/ReachyMini-iOS.xcarchive
33	
34	set -o pipefail
35	# COMPILATION_CACHE_ENABLE_CACHING=NO: the shipping artifact gets a clean,
36	# uncached compile. The cache went on by default the day before 0.1.1 was
37	# archived, and 0.1.1 is the build that installed from TestFlight with no
38	# Shortcuts actions at all — an archive is rare enough that replayed
39	# compilations buy nothing worth that variable. The metadata check below is
40	# what proves the archive either way, before anything is uploaded.
41	xcodebuild archive \
42	  -workspace Apps/ReachyMiniApps.xcworkspace -scheme ReachyMini \
43	  -destination 'generic/platform=iOS' -configuration Release \
44	  -archivePath "$ARCHIVE" -derivedDataPath Apps/DerivedData \
45	  DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="$REACHY_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM" CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Automatic \
46	  CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION="$BUILD_NUMBER" \
47	  COMPILATION_CACHE_ENABLE_CACHING=NO \
48	  -allowProvisioningUpdates \
49	  -skipPackagePluginValidation -skipMacroValidation \
50	  2>&1 | xcsift
51	
52	# An archive whose Metadata.appintents came out empty ships an app with no
53	# actions in the Shortcuts app, and nothing in the build reddens over it.
54	Scripts/check-appintents-metadata.sh "$ARCHIVE"
55	
56	EXPORT_OPTIONS="$(appstore_export_options "$upload")"
57	
58	xcodebuild -exportArchive \
59	  -archivePath "$ARCHIVE" \
60	  -exportOptionsPlist "$EXPORT_OPTIONS" \
61	  -exportPath Apps/DerivedData/Export/iOS \
62	  -allowProvisioningUpdates \
63	  2>&1 | xcsift
64	
65	if [ "$upload" = true ]; then
66	  echo "Uploaded build $BUILD_NUMBER to App Store Connect. TestFlight shows it after processing (minutes)."
67	else
68	  # The archive was already checked, but the .ipa is what actually ships, and
69	  # -exportArchive re-signs and repacks on the way — so prove the metadata
70	  # survived the export too. Only the --no-upload path leaves an .ipa behind;
71	  # `destination: upload` hands the artifact straight to App Store Connect.
72	  IPA="$(ls Apps/DerivedData/Export/iOS/*.ipa | head -1)"
